headline: BI's 25bp hike to 6.00% leaves the 1Y unmoved (−1.1bp) but pushes the 3–5Y up 3.5–4.0bp and the 10Y to 7.73%, its highest since at least Nov 2021, despite a 2bp Treasury rally; JISDOR eases to 18,252 and the daily flow signal is −0.79
summary: PHEI's IGSYC bear-steepened through the belly after BI's hike: the 1Y slipped 1.1bp to 6.709% and the 1M 1.4bp to 6.162%, while the 2Y rose 1.7bp to 7.028%, the 3Y 3.5bp to 7.258%, the 5Y 3.7bp to 7.550% and the 10Y 1.1bp to 7.729%, the highest on the dashboard's history since Nov 2021. 2s5s widened 2.0bp to 52.2bp and 1s2s 2.8bp to 31.9bp, both the widest of 15 stored days, and the 2s5s10s fly rose 4.5bp to 34.3bp; 5s10s flattened 2.5bp to 17.9bp. With the BI-Rate 25bp higher, the 1Y now sits only 70.9bp over it, the narrowest stored. FR0109 lost 2.6bp to 7.557% (8.4bp cheap to the curve) and FR0108 6.3bp to 7.725% (on the curve, from 5.1bp rich); the fitted PBS 5Y moved to 0.8bp through IGSYC from 0.4bp over, the retail fit is 14.3bp rich at 5Y, and PHEI's corporate curves moved with IGSYC, leaving AAA 3Y at 48.7bp over.
drivers: BI hiked 25bp; the belly took it

Bank Indonesia raised the BI-Rate to 6.00% and the deposit and lending facilities to 5.25% and 6.75%, its fourth hike this year and 125bp since May; Reuters' poll had 10 of 27 economists expecting it, so most saw a hold. BI also sweetened DNDF hedging incentives (premium discounts to 45% at 6 months and 50% at 12 months). The 1M and 1Y fell 1.1–1.4bp, so the front end had largely priced the move, while the 3–5Y rose 3.5–4.0bp; analysts at Barclays and Capital Economics now pencil in a 6.50–6.75% peak, which is what the belly appears to be pricing.

JISDOR fixed 0.07% firmer at 18,252 after Tuesday's 18,264 record, and spot closed 0.13% stronger at 18,232 (Kontan, Bloomberg data). That is a small move for a hike, and JISDOR is still 0.63% weaker this month; whether BI's step brings foreign bond buyers back is not yet visible in published data. BI says Q4 portfolio flows to Nov 16 are a net $4.8bn inflow, led by the government's global bonds and sukuk and SBN, against a $0.9bn equity outflow; that does not rule out selling since.
Treasuries rallied again; INDOGBs did not follow

The US 10Y fell about 2bp on Tuesday to 5.10% after in-line October retail sales (+0.2% m/m) and softer stocks. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.28 that implies −0.6bp for the INDOGB 10Y; it rose 1.1bp, so Treasuries explain none of today's move. The INDOGB − UST spread widened to 262.9bp from 259.8bp (81st percentile of 52 weeks, range 191–286bp), a nominal pick-up before currency risk.
Stocks sold off after the decision

The JCI reversed from an intraday high of 5,374 to close 1.07% lower at 5,247.88, with materials, energy and industrials down 2.7–3.0% (Kontan). Foreigners were net sellers of Rp338bn in the morning session (CNBC Indonesia, Stockbit data); a full-day count was not in my sources. Over 20 sessions the JCI is down 13.9% and USD/IDR up 1.97%, which keeps the equity and rupiah parts of the flow signal bearish.

view: BI has bought the rupiah some time, but the curve says the market expects more: the 1Y held while the 3–5Y cheapened and 2s5s hit 52.2bp, and the 10Y at 7.729% sits 2.1bp under my 7.75% underweight trigger with Treasuries giving no help. The daily Bond Flow Signal is −0.79 (sell-off; −0.86 yesterday on today's rebuild): the 10Y trend part is the most bearish (z +1.60, +48.1bp over 20 sessions), then the JCI (z −1.38, −13.9%) and the rupiah (z +0.75, +1.97%), while the spread, 16.2bp above its 130-day average (z +0.57), leans bond-bullish; the daily build's sell-off episode runs from Sep 28 (28 sessions, +52.2bp). Since July 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 0.80 outright (200.7bp) and 0.85 hedged against Treasuries (208.3bp), against −44.1bp for holding the 10Y, but sell-off calls were right only 52.1% of the time over the next 20 sessions (hedged 51.6%; rally calls 57.9%, hedged 64.8%) and the 10Y fell 0.2bp on average after them; on the same daily build the outright Sharpe was 1.01 in Jul 2022–Aug 2024 and 0.65 since. The weekly build scores 0.57 and 0.75; a variant using the US 10Y trend reaches 0.92 and 0.95 on the weekly build but was chosen after the fact and is not live, and all of these are in-sample back-tests. Over four weeks the INDOGB 10Y is up 27.2bp and the US 10Y 14bp, yet at the weekly beta of −0.12 the Treasury-linked part is −1.7bp and +28.9bp is residual, the part Treasuries do not explain. I stay neutral on the 10Y in a 7.60–7.85% range, keep the 5Y as the curve trade now that BI has moved (buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70%, 4bp away), and keep the 1Y, only 71bp over the new BI-Rate, as the bucket with the least cushion.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The hike lifted the BI-Rate to 6.00% while the IGSYC 1Y slipped 1.1bp to 6.709%, so the spread collapsed 26.1bp to 70.9bp, the narrowest of 15 stored days (7th percentile, average 105.1bp); the 2Y rose 1.7bp to 7.028%, 102.8bp over. The 3M (0.25Y) is 6.26% and the 1M 6.16%, just 16bp over the policy rate. The previous 7.10% add level was not reached (39bp away); no position. Yesterday's warning that a hike would leave the 1Y ~72bp over the rate was borne out.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y at 1Y 7.00% (lowered from 7.10% for a reason: it is now 100bp over the new BI-Rate, near the stored average), target 6.75%, stop 7.25%; the bucket stays most exposed to a December hike.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109 / PBS040)
buckets.why: The IGSYC 5Y rose 3.7bp to 7.550% (80th percentile of 15 stored days, average 7.497%), +8.1bp this week, and the 2s5s10s fly rose 4.5bp to 34.3bp (80th percentile, average 26.2bp). FR0109 lost 2.6bp to 7.557% and is 8.4bp cheap to the curve. BI has now hiked, meeting the trigger, but FR0109's entry (7.60–7.70%) is 4.3bp away and not filled.
buckets.call: Keep: buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70%; target 7.35%, stop 7.95%. The belly carries the hike premium the front end does not.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The IGSYC 10Y rose 1.1bp to 7.729%, the top of the past year (100th percentile of 178 days, average 6.87%) and of the stored history since Nov 2021, against a 2bp US rally. The signal is −0.79, but the underweight rule also needs a 10Y close above 7.75%, 2.1bp away, so it is not triggered. FR0108 rose 6.3bp to 7.725% and is now on the curve after 5.1bp rich.
buckets.call: Neutral, range 7.60–7.85% (raised 5bp: the 10Y has held above 7.60% all week). Underweight if the signal stays below −0.5 and the 10Y closes above 7.75%; tactical long only above 7.85% (stop 8.05%) or once the signal is above 0 with JISDOR below 18,000.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC 10s20s is 1.0bp (40th percentile of 15 stored days, average 1.4bp, range 0.1–2.9bp); the long end is flat. The benchmark spread FR0107 − FR0108 narrowed to 0.2bp from 4.7bp as FR0108 lost 6.3bp and FR0107 1.9bp, now 5.2bp from the −5bp re-entry.
buckets.call: Wait. Re-enter the FR0108/FR0107 steepener duration-weighted at −5bp or lower, target +5bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.stance: Hold FR over PBS034; PBS040 entered
buckets.why: The fitted PBS 5Y is 0.8bp through IGSYC (43rd percentile of 14 stored days, average −1.5bp), back from yesterday's 0.4bp over; the fit rests on four series (level −2.8bp, slope 5.5bp), so confidence is limited. PBS034 fell 1.7bp to 7.683% and is 3.5bp rich; on the benchmark-history measure its richness rose 2.5bp, a 2.5bp loss for the FR-over-PBS034 switch, which stays open with the switch-back (PBS034 5bp cheap) 8.5bp away. The PBS040 add zone was live at Tuesday's 7.519% close; PBS040 is now 7.552%, 3.3bp against, and 12.8bp cheap to the curve.
buckets.call: Hold FR over PBS034; switch back once PBS034 is 5bp cheap to IGSYC. Hold PBS040 from 7.52%: target 7.30%, stop 7.80%.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y rose 3.5bp to 7.745%, matching IGSYC, so the spread held at 48.7bp, the narrowest of 14 stored days (14th percentile, average 50.1bp). AA is 90.2bp over (86th percentile, average 86.6bp), A 151.6bp and BBB 223.2bp over AA (21st percentile, average 237.5bp). Fourteen days is a thin base, and PHEI's corporate curves move almost one-for-one with IGSYC day to day; the add level (AAA 3Y past 70bp) was not reached.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB while funding costs rise with the BI-Rate.

buckets.name: Retail SBN 5Y (ORI/SR)
buckets.why: The fitted retail curve is 14.3bp through IGSYC at 5Y (50th percentile of 14 stored days, average −13.4bp) and 5.3bp over at 2Y; the fit uses 25 series with a 74bp slope, so part of this is fit artefact. Secondary spreads run from 52bp rich (SR024T3) to 64bp cheap (ORI027T3, which lost 16.4bp to 7.58%); ORI026T6 is 7.666%, 34bp over. ST017 (open to Dec 2) floors at 6.95% (2Y) and 7.05% (4Y), now below the IGSYC 2Y (7.03%).
buckets.call: New money: FR0109 or PBS040 for liquidity; ST017 for hold-to-maturity buyers who want further BI-hike upside. Buy secondary retail only at the cheap end (ORI026T6, ~34bp over).

watch: Next: FOMC minutes and Nvidia results (Wed Nov 18, New York), Indonesia's Q3 balance of payments (Fri Nov 20), the next SUN auction as the first test of demand after the hike, MSCI changes after the Nov 30 close, the ST017 book closing Dec 2, the Fed decision on Dec 9 and FTSE deletions on Dec 21; a 10Y close above 7.75% would trigger the underweight, while JISDOR back below 18,000 would argue against a December BI hike.
